segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And they paraded him around to the doors of the churches,
mocking and scoffing at the Christians.
Now the oppression and wrath which the people of Mosul endured during these two months,
no tongue is able to utter,
nor any pen to record.
Awake now, and sleep not, O Lord!
And see the blood of Your servants that is shed without mercy,
and have pity on Your church and on Your flock, which is trampled underfoot by persecutors! And in those days when Buqa was killed,
and Baytmish was sent to these western regions,
and they mounted all the forces of the Mongols to conquer Arghun,
those who were in Syria became alarmed,
and terror, fear, and trembling fell upon them,
and they thought that they were going to come against them.
And so they too gathered strength,
and assembled many forces,
and made ready for an encounter.
And when they were confirmed [in their knowledge]
that the Mongols were occupied with each other,
and cared nothing about others,
they did not allow their gathering to be dissolved in vain.
They went and encamped against Tripoli, the city on the shore of the Great Sea,
and waged a fierce war against it.
And those inside sent and sought help from their Frankish kinsmen on the island of Cyprus,
and a few were sent to them by means of ships over the sea.
And when they arrived,
the people of the city also took courage and stood upon the walls,
and fought with those outside more vigorously for nearly three months, more or less.
And when those outside prevailed,
and breached its wall with mangonels,
and the Christians {OCR?} saw that they were overcome by those outside,
most of them boarded the ships,
and departed and went to Cyprus.
And as for the rest who remained in the city,
the Arabs entered against them,
drew their swords,
and mingled with one another,
and they killed and were killed.
And on account of the great slaughter that occurred among the Arabs,
they were inflamed with fury,
and destroyed the wretched city completely,
and left in it no citadel or church that they did not demolish.
And they carried off from it vast, boundless wealth,
and took captive sons and daughters without number,
and slaughtered priests, deacons, monks, and nuns whose number has no end,
and they left it desolate and departed.
These things happened at the middle of Nisan,
